newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - U.S. durable goods seen up 0.6 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - U.S. durable goods seen up 0.6 pct in May.

text.p: U.S. durable goods orders were seen rising by 0.6 percent in May following a 1.3 percent increase in April, economists surveyed by Reuters said.
However, views varied as to how much economic slowing would be evident in the number, to be released Wednesday at 830 EDT/1230 GMT by the Commerce Department.
"We see durable goods up 0.3 percent. Orders should be right on trend," said Jerry Zukowski, economist at PaineWebber Inc.
Zukowski said defense orders looked to be well behaved, but acknowledged the orders statistic could be volatile. "We're right on trend other than the inherent volatility of the number," he said.
The fundamentals of the economy pointed to a clear uptrend in orders, especially in the business and equipment sectors of the report, Zukowski said.

However, Kathleen Stephansen, senior economist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, disagreed. Her firm was calling for a small decline of 0.2 percent following the strong figure seen in April, she said.
"We see this number marginally retracing. But even with this (weaker) number there's still momentum in production," Stephansen said.
She saw gross domestic product slowing to a 1.0 percent rate -- markedly down from the first quarter.
Mary Dennis, senior economist at Merrill Lynch & Co, saw durable goods remaining unchanged in May.
"I don't think the economy is slowing, but aircraft orders are exceptionally weak," Dennis said.

While not usually a major market mover, durable goods likely would weigh on the view held by Federal Reserve policy makers on the strength of the manufacturing sector of the economy. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan has stated the central bank would be looking for a deceleration in growth rather than overt signs of inflation in determining the course of future monetary policy.
